S42.01.needs: A signed-in AGI Cloud account, on a plan that allows scheduled tasks.
S42.01.note: A second route is Schedules > Try a template > 'Daily briefing' (the template from packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/schedules.ts), which then needs Create Schedule. The delivery itself runs on the server and is not visible in the code, so the tester must wait for a run.
steps: Sign in to AGI Cloud, then open the side menu and tap Settings.
Tap Notifications.
Turn on the Daily brief switch. Wait for the row 'Daily brief time, 08:00' to appear.
Open Schedules from the side menu and look for a schedule named Daily brief, which the app should have created. Compare with Expected: a recurring daily briefing is set up.
S42.01.where: Side menu > Settings > Notifications > Daily brief (turn the switch on)

S42.04.needs: A signed-in AGI Cloud account, on a plan that allows scheduled tasks.
S42.04.note: The Daily brief time in Settings > Notifications offers only 07:00, 08:00 and 09:00 and uses the device time zone, with no time zone control. The zone can be set only on a schedule form.
steps: Open the side menu and tap Schedules, then tap Create schedule.
Set Recurrence to Daily and tap the Preferred time field to pick a time.
Scroll to the Time zone field and tap it. Pick a different zone from the list.
Tap Create Schedule and open the new schedule. Compare with Expected: the time and time zone you chose are shown.
S42.04.where: Side menu > Schedules > Create Schedule (form) > Preferred time and Time zone

S42.15.needs: A schedule already set up (for example Daily brief) on a signed-in AGI Cloud account.
S42.15.note: A schedule paused for approval cannot be resumed from the card. The card says 'Paused for your approval, so approve or deny it in History.' instead.
steps: Open the side menu and tap Schedules. Make sure at least one schedule exists, such as Daily brief.
Tap the switch on a schedule card to turn it off, or tap its More actions button and choose Pause.
Look at the card: it should show as paused, and the Paused filter should list it.
Tap the switch again, or choose Resume from More actions. Compare with Expected: the schedule pauses and resumes.
S42.15.where: Side menu > Schedules > (a schedule card) > switch on the card, or More actions > Pause / Resume

S42.16.needs: None for the setting. Holding push notifications needs a second device or push delivery, which the tester cannot see from the app.
S42.16.note: The holding of push notifications and nudges happens on the server (apps/web/lib/services/quiet-hours-service.ts). The app shows no visible sign of the hold, so only the setting and the on-screen alert can be checked from the UI.
steps: Open Settings, tap Time and focus.
Turn on Enable quiet hours, then set the Days, Start time and End time so the current time falls inside the window.
Return to the app or switch away and back during that window.
Look for the alert 'Quiet hours are active' with the text 'This is a reminder, not a lock.' Compare with Expected: quiet hours are active on the device.
S42.16.where: Side menu > Settings > Time and focus > Quiet hours > Enable quiet hours

S42.17.needs: A phone that allows notifications for the app, and a schedule to run (or an agent task).
S42.17.note: Agent-task completion falls under Task and approval updates, which says 'finished or failed tasks'.
steps: Open Settings, tap Notifications. Turn on notifications if it asks.
Find the row Scheduled tasks, described as 'When a scheduled task runs, finishes or needs you', and set it on.
On a schedule card, tap More actions and choose Run now, then wait for the run to finish.
Look for a phone notification when the run completes. Compare with Expected: the user is notified when background work completes.
S42.17.where: Side menu > Settings > Notifications > Scheduled tasks (and Task and approval updates)

S42.19.needs: A signed-in AGI Cloud account. Reflect may ask for memory to be on (ReflectMemoryRequiredError).
S42.19.note: Reflect needs a signed-in cloud account and may show a memory-required message; the exact wording was not checked.
steps: Open Settings and tap Reflect. Sign in if asked.
Wait for 'Building your recap…' to finish.
Read the headline, the period label and the stats (Conversations, Active days, Most active day, Peak start time).
Compare with Expected: a reflection on how the user uses the product is shown.
S42.19.where: Side menu > Settings > Reflect (shows the page titled Reflect, with range choices 30 days, 3 months, 6 months, 1 year)

S42.21.needs: A signed-in AGI Cloud account with enough chat history for the past year.
S42.21.note: No screen or label named 'Annual recap' exists. The past-year recap is the 1 year range on Reflect, and the 365-day option is labelled '1 year'.
steps: Open Settings and tap Reflect.
Tap the range choice 1 year (accessibility label 'Show the past 1 year').
Wait for the recap to load and read its period label, headline and stats.
Compare with Expected: a recap of the past year is shown.

S42.22.needs: None. Use the app for the full chosen time, or pick 30 minutes to shorten the test.
S42.22.note: The reminder counts active app time. The menu choices are Off, 30 minutes, 1 hour, 2 hours and 4 hours.
steps: Open Settings, tap Time and focus, then tap the Break reminders row.
Choose a time, such as 30 minutes, from the menu. The row then reads 'After 30 min'.
Keep using the app until about that much time has passed in one day.
Look for the alert 'Time for a break?' with 'You have spent about 30 minutes in AGI today.' Compare with Expected.
S42.22.where: Side menu > Settings > Time and focus > Break reminders

S42.23.note: The same page can also be reached from Settings > Notifications > Quiet hours (the row reads 'Quiet hours. On' or 'Off').
steps: Open the side menu, tap Settings, then tap Time and focus.
Look for the section Break reminders with its row, and the section Quiet hours with Enable quiet hours.
Change one value, go back, and open the page again.
Compare with Expected: the page holds break reminders and quiet hours, and the change is kept.
S42.23.where: Side menu > Settings > Time and focus

S42.25.needs: A schedule that has already run at least once (use Run now on a schedule card).
S42.25.note: No label named 'saved editions' was found. The run list is the closest match, and the tester should check that past outputs can be opened.
steps: Open the side menu and tap Schedules.
Tap the Scheduled runs button in the header.
Scroll the list of past runs. Compare with Expected: past outputs are kept as a browsable history.
Go back, tap More actions on a schedule card and choose Show history. Look for the heading Run History with the last runs.
S42.25.where: Side menu > Schedules > Scheduled runs (header button); or on a schedule card, More actions > Show history
